1926.event: The Comet of Conquest is Halley's Comet as it appeared over England in the spring of 1066. That autumn, Duke William of Normandy would invade and defeat King Harold at Hastings, but in April all England could do was stare at the burning star. Both sides read it as an omen. The English feared it foretold the doom of Harold. The Normans hoped it promised the triumph of William. The Bayeux Tapestry, sewn to tell the story of the conquest, shows frightened men pointing at the comet, with words in Latin saying they marvel at the star. The comet was only ice and dust swinging past the sun. But believed hard enough, an omen has a way of coming true.
1926.announce: Here is a verse about the burning star that both armies read as an omen: The Comet of Conquest.
1926.title: The Comet of Conquest
1926.piece:
It hung over England for a week,
Halley's Comet, blazing in the spring sky,
and everyone knew what it meant.
Everyone always knows what comets mean:
disaster, death, the fall of kings.
I stood in a Sussex field and watched the villagers
point at it with white faces.
The English said it foretold the doom of Harold.
The Normans said it foretold the triumph of William.
The Bayeux Tapestry sewed it into the story for all time:
men staring up at the burning star,
marveling, as the old Latin says, at the star.
It was only ice and dust, swinging past the sun.
But in 1066 it was an omen,
and omens, believed hard enough, have a way of coming true.
